title: Uncovering cancer vulnerabilities by machine learning prediction of synthetic lethality.
summary: PARIS inferred synthetic-lethal interactions from DepMap CRISPR and multi-omic data. Follow-up CRISPR assays supported an ALDH2-BRIP1 dependency in low-ALDH2 cancer-cell models; this is preclinical cell evidence, not patient stratification or treatment benefit.
organization: BioMed X; University Hospital Heidelberg; National Center for Tumor Diseases

evidence.tested: PARIS predicted 15 high-confidence interactions across 549 DNA-damage-repair genes. Experimental follow-up tested ALDH2-BRIP1 in breast cancer cell lines and engineered RPE-1 cells using CRISPR knockouts, colony formation and DNA-damage readouts. The paper separately reports experimental validation of CDKN2A-TYMP-TYMS.
evidence.unknown: Validation was in cell models and does not establish patient stratification or treatment benefit. The authors note heterozygous Fanconi-anemia-pathway mutations in several cancer lines as a possible background confounder.
evidence.ai_role: PARIS uses random-forest importance scores and Boruta feature selection to explain CRISPR dependency scores from mutation and expression features across DepMap cell lines, then ranks candidate synthetic-lethal interactions.

source_review.scope: Full PMC paper, including model description, experimental methods, results and discussion.
